concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: As of 15 September 2026, the original DPA required notification without undue delay and no later than 48 hours after the Processor became aware of a breach. The amendment reducing this period to 24 hours did not take effect until 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment effective 1 October 2026 replaced the 48-hour period with a requirement to notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after awareness of a breach.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: For routine on-site audits after the amendment took effect, the audit protocol requires at least 10 Business Days' notice. This more specific protocol applies to on-site audits and sets the applicable minimum notice period.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: As of 1 November 2026, the amended liability clause capped the Processor's aggregate liability for DPA breaches at EUR 1,000,000. This cap applies regardless of the EUR 700,000 in fees because the amended clause no longer uses the higher-of-fees formulation.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: The amended liability clause expressly states that the EUR 1,000,000 cap does not apply to breaches of the confidentiality obligations.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd was listed as an approved Sub-processor in Annex 3, and its approval was not withdrawn until 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: The amendment provides that Meridian Mail Ltd's approval was withdrawn with effect from 1 January 2027, so it was not approved on 1 February 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, Personal Data was stored or processed in Norway and Estonia under the original DPA, and in Ireland and Lithuania through the approved Sub-processors. These are four distinct countries.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: For a termination on 31 December 2026, the amended deletion period was 60 days. The 60-day period ends on 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach. the notice must describe the breach, affected data subjects and records, likely consequences, and response or mitigation measures, while the processor must also document the breach and cooperate with required regulatory or data-subject notifications.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach. The notice must describe the breach, affected data subjects and records, likely consequences, and response or mitigation measures, while the Processor must also document the breach and cooperate with required regulatory or data-subject notifications.
justifications: The amended breach-notification clause sets a 24-hour outer deadline while retaining the separate duty to act without undue delay. The original content, documentation, and cooperation requirements remain in force.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: The breach involved confirmed exposure of usable privileged credentials, which triggers the expedited 12-hour initial-notification limit.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Awareness began at 17:10 on 9 April, and the notice was delivered at 06:00 on 10 April, exceeding the applicable 12-hour outer limit by 50 minutes.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: The third Business Day after awareness is calculated from 9 April, excluding the closure day on 12 April and the single approved pause day on 14 April; the deadline therefore falls at the end of 16 April.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: The ordinary deletion deadline is 29 August 2027, but the last applicable hold ends on 25 August and requires deletion by the later of that deadline and the end of the tenth Business Day after release. The tenth Business Day is 9 September 2027.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: The backup was created on 30 June 2027 and contains no held records. Its deadline is the earlier of the ordinary deletion deadline and 35 calendar days after creation, which is 4 August 2027.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: On 1 September 2027, the records remain retained under the hold and may be used only for legal preservation, not service delivery or analytics.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval could begin only after the proposed start date, written consent, and completed security review, whichever was latest. The security review completed on 22 April 2027, and processing began that day.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Cendrillon Mail SAS was approved for transactional email from France and continued providing ordinary transactional email. Meridian Mail Ltd's emergency permission did not reinstate its authorisation for ordinary customer email.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: On 15 May 2027, actual processing and effective authorisation were established for existing storage in Norway and Estonia, monitoring in Lithuania, ordinary transactional email in France, and Nordlicht infrastructure processing in Sweden. Finland, Denmark, Germany, and Ireland did not meet both conditions on that date.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: Qualifying fees are EUR 1,140,000 after removing VAT and the service credit, so twice the fees is EUR 2,280,000, which exceeds the EUR 2,000,000 minimum security cap.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The EUR 1,000,000 ordinary cap is reduced by EUR 300,000 in earlier ordinary payments, leaving EUR 700,000 available.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: Payable amounts are EUR 700,000 for the ordinary claim, EUR 1,750,000 for the single shared security loss, and EUR 350,000 for the two confidentiality losses, totaling EUR 2,800,000.
